db_evidence.notes: The text-side memory DB (episodes, semantic_triples, event_steps, visual_clips captions) only has coarse 30-second-granularity summaries for this fight (e.g. 'barry battles large furry ape-like boss', 'barry defeats ape-like boss') and no per-skill-cast rows at all; semantic_triples has zero rows between 20400 and 20580. Every rollout therefore had to rely entirely on clip_qa (visual sub-agent) to resolve the skill-cast order -- there was no textual fallback to catch or correct a visual misread. Frame checks I performed confirm the four clue intervals do correspond to genuine, visually distinct player skill-cast moments (Immobilize ~20460-465, Shenfa doubles ~20462-465, Hundred-Eyed spirit transformation ~20485-490, Red Tides fiery transformation ~20546-558), i.e. the ground truth is retrievable but only via careful visual inspection, not via SQL/semantic search.

root_causes: The boss (Mad Tiger) has a self-triggered red glowing chest-explosion attack at ~20400-20430 s that visually resembles a dramatic player skill-cast VFX; the clip_qa sub-agent repeatedly misidentified this enemy attack as a player skill (Hundred-Eyed spirit or Immobilize/Red Tides) in rollouts 1 and 2, and a similar early misread (~20452-455) affected rollout 4, anchoring the reported order 20-60s earlier than the true clue intervals.

The two 'transformation' skills (Red Tides / 变身广智 and Hundred-Eyed Daoist Master spirit / 百目真人精魄) produce visually similar dramatic transformation effects late in the fight (~20485-490 and ~20546-558) and were swapped by clip_qa in rollouts 0 and 2, flipping the last one or two answer positions.

clip_qa window choice mattered: rollouts that scanned starting at 20400 (including the boss's opening-attack noise) were more prone to false-positive early skill detections than rollout 3, which started its single window at 20430, just past that noisy region.

No textual/DB evidence exists at fine enough granularity to cross-check or override a wrong clip_qa reading, so a single visual misidentification directly became the final wrong answer in the affected rollouts.
what_worked: Rollout 3's clip_qa window (20430-20580) excluded the boss's opening-attack VFX at 20400-20430 that misled other rollouts, and got all four skills' relative order right in a single call.

Rollout 4's targeted follow-up clip_qa call explicitly asking to distinguish the two transformation effects (spirit vs Red Tides) frame-by-frame correctly resolved that specific ambiguity, even though an earlier unrelated misread still cost it points.
All rollouts correctly followed the 'HUD icon lit is not proof of cast' instruction from the visual-verification skill, focusing on visible cast effects rather than skill-wheel highlighting.
transferable_lessons: For boss-fight skill-ordering questions, do not start the clip_qa scan window at the very beginning of the encounter by default; a wide net that includes pre-engagement or opening-attack frames increases the chance the visual sub-agent misattributes enemy VFX to the player.

When two candidate skills produce visually similar 'transformation' effects, issue a dedicated clip_qa call asking it to explicitly compare and name the distinguishing visual cues (weapon type, character silhouette/species, color) between the two specific moments, rather than a single broad scan covering all four skills at once.

Treat a clip_qa report of a skill cast happening unusually early (e.g. within the first few seconds of a boss encounter, before any other skill has plausibly been used) as a red flag worth a second, narrower verification pass rather than accepting it at face value.

Because coarse-grained textual memory (30s-episode captions) is the only DB coverage available for fast in-combat skill sequences, do not expect SQL/semantic_search to adjudicate a visual ordering disagreement -- budget for iterative, narrowing clip_qa calls instead.
open_questions: Whether the judge scores purely on the reported 1-2-3-4 order string or also partially credits partially-correct orders/timestamps (rollout 3's exact timestamps for skills 4 and 1 do not match my directly-verified ground truth (~20485-490 and ~20546-558) even though its stated order was correct, and it still scored a full 5).

Whether the ~20452-455 effect that misled rollout 4 into placing Shenfa too early is the same boss opening-attack VFX confirmed at 20426-20430, or a distinct visual confound; I did not pull a frame at exactly that timestamp to confirm.
